title: Appendix C - Sources, tools and certifications for the B2

blocks.text: Appendix C - Sources, tools and certifications for the B2

These resources support the course; They don't replace him. Added to Appendix C of Volumes 2, 3 and 4 (grammar, dictionaries by root, Communicate in Arabic B1-B2, Al Jazeera Learning Arabic, Monte Carlo Doualiya, Kallimni ʿArabi, CIMA), which remain valid. Each tab indicates recipients, level, advantages, limits, cost and way of use. The information has been checked on the pages indicated as source on 26 October 2026. Prices, editions, schedules, addresses and availability change: check them again before buying or signing up. When a data was not indicated in a reliable source, the card says so. How to choose. In B2 need four things: one or two heads to read every day, a source of listening in fuṣḥā at natural speed, a news verification platform for the INT track, and authentic material in varieties (Egyptian, Levantine, Moroccan). The sections books C1 and C2 are optional: they are for those who want more translation exercise or a more extensive media lexicon. Rule for authentic texts. Readings of different editorial lines (B2-19), notes always tested, date and address, and applies the reading method (B2-01) and verification (INT-05). The rules of the INT track also apply here: only public sources, language method, no research on private citizens.
C1 · Books for the B2
Media Arabic (series ............) Elisabeth Kendall · Edinburgh University Press, second edition revised and updated, 2012 · ISBN 9780748644964 (ebook).
• Recipients: who reads and translates the Arab press, in both directions.
• Level: the editor's page does not indicate a level; the vocabulary corresponds to that of the forms B2.1 and B2.2.

• Advantages: thematic vocabulary in eight areas (general: news, statements, sources and media idioms; policy and government; elections; military field; public order and justice; economy; trade and industry; aid and development); English-Arabic index and audio files for pronunciation in the second edition; about 112 pages.
• Limits: in English; is a vocabulary, not a course (no texts or exercises); the page consulted indicates only the ISBN of the ebook.
• Cost: not indicated on the page consulted.
• Use during the course: as a review of the vocabulary for areas of B2-24 and as quick control while reading authentic texts; next B2-03 → B2-06 and INT-03INT-04.
Source: degruyterbrill.com (book tab, DOI 10.1515/9780748644964)

Thinking Arabic Translation · A Course in Translation Method: Arabic to English James Dickins, Sándor Hervey, Ian Higgins · Routledge, Necklace "Thinking Translation" second edition, 2016 (copyright 2017) · ISBN 9780415705639.
• Target group: who wants to improve translation from Arabic and advanced students thinking about a job from translators.
• Level: advanced; appropriate from the end of B2 Then.

• Advantages: a method, not just examples; chapters with explanations, discussion and exercises on full texts of many genres (days, narrative, political discourses, constitutions, technical texts); themes close to the module B2.3: revision, genre, meaning denotative and connotative, parallelism, metaphor, linguistic variety (record and dialect); 332 pages.
• Limits: the language of arrival is English, not Italian; The principles apply, the solutions need to be adapted.
• Cost: The page of the publisher consulted does not show the price.
• Use during: after B2-13 and B2-14, chapters on connotation, metaphor and linguistic variety as deepening; in preparation for C1, exercises on whole texts.
• Source: routedge.com (book tab)
Al-Kitaab fii Taʿallum al-ʿArabiyya · Part Three Kristen Brustad, Mahmoud Al-Batal, Abbas Al-Tonsi · Georgetown University Press, 2007 · ISBN 9781589011496 (brossura).
• Targets: those who have finished an intermediate-advanced path and want to move to the upper level.
• Level: the editor indicates as objective the level of the ACTFL scale: for this course it is a bridge towards the C1, not a book of B2.

• Advantages: over thirty authentic texts by authors from all over the Arab world (politics, society, religion, literature), of different genres, styles and epochs; work on vocabulary, sentence structure and verb; much writing; Egyptian video material; streaming audio and video on the publisher's website; 424 pages.
• Limits: in English; difficult texts for those who have just arrived at the B2; part of the additional material requires a request for access.
• Cost: USD 69,95 (Publisher's price, paperback).
• Use during the course: after examination B2, awaiting Volume 6; literary texts anticipate the C1.
• Source: press.georgietown.edu (book tab)

Communicate in Arabic · Levels B1-B2 (Hoepli, 2024). The card is in Appendix C of the Volume 4. In B2 The second half is used: the units on migrants and refugees, media, politics, the digital world and the economy are alongside B2-03, B2-19 and B2-20.
C2 · Dictionaries and vocabulary tools

Dictionaries by root (Hans Wehr, Baldissera: Volumes 3 and 4). The translation tool remains; tests and examinations shall be permitted only in translation tests. Doha Historical Dictionary of Arabic ( ⁧معجم الدوحة التاريخي للغة العربية⁩ ) · dohadictionary.org.

• What is it: an Arabic historical dictionary documenting, with dated quotations and sources, the first attestation of every word and the evolution of its meanings in about two thousand years; includes comparisons with other Semitic languages and the etymology of loans.
• Who cares: the Arab Center for Research and Policy Studies in Doha; the completion was announced on
27 November 2025, with an open and updated online platform.
• Limits: is a search tool, not a dictionary of use; the sources consulted do not explicitly state whether access is free.
• Use during the course: for curiosity and for the C1; in B2 can help to understand why an ancient word makes sense new (B2-19, neologisms: ⁧تَغْرِيدَة⁩ , ⁧وَسْم⁩ ).
• Sources: dohainstitute.org (communicato del 27 November 2025); ajnet.me 21 December 2025, that indicates the site). The Living Arabic Project · Lughatuna · livingarabic.com.
• What is it: online dictionaries and apps for the fuṣḥā and for different varieties: Egyptian, Levantine (Arabic-English and Arab-Arab), North African, Gulf, Iraqi, Sudanese, Yemeni.
• Advantages: research by Arabic word, English word or root; vowels, plurals, notes of pronunciation and examples.

• Limits: in English; the page does not say if the site is free; the Lughatuna app is paid; the project was born by a list of words compiled by a student and edited by a small company (Lughatuna LLC): controls the important words with a speaker.
• Use during the course: for dialect words of listening B2-17, B2-18 and B2-21 and EGY and MAG tracks.
Source: livingarabic.com

Egyptian: Hinds and Badawi, A Dictionary of Egyptian Arabic. It is the most complete dictionary of the Egyptian, ordained by root; has not been updated, but remains the reference; According to the guide consulted, there is an online version available on ejtaal.net. Source: arabic-for-nerds.com (-) The Ultimate Guide to Arabic Dialect Dictionaries. Moroccan: two dictionaries of Georgetown University Press.

• The Georgetown Dictionary of Moroccan Arabic (2019ISBN 9781626163317, 760 Pages): over 13.000 Moroccan-English voices and 8.000 English-Moroccan; voices in Arabic characters sorted by root, with international phonetic alphabet pronunciation; loans from French, Spanish and amazigh; many examples. It is the best choice for those who continue with the Moroccan. Source: campusbokhandeln.se (bibliographic card).

• A Dictionary of Moroccan Arabic (ed. Harrell and Harvey Sobelman; edition in the necklace "Georgetown Classics in Arabic Languages and Linguistics" ISBN 9781589011038, 528 pages, USD 54,95 in paperback): the classic first published in 1966, based on the spoken language of Fès, Rabat and Casablanca; examples, formulas and idioms of everyday life; The words are in transcription. Source: press.georgietown.edu.
• Use during: for MAG-01 MAG-04 the vocabulary of units and the tutor are sufficient; the dictionary serves after B2, if the Moroccan trace continues.
C3 · News to read and listen to

UN News in Arabic ( ⁧أخبار الأمم المتحدة⁩ ) · news.un.org/ar. The Arabic editorial staff of the United Nations news publishes daily (daily news comes out in eight languages, including Arabic) and has a podcast in Arabic, ... ⁧أخبار الأمم المتحدة⁩ - ⁧منظور عالمي قصص إنسانية⁩ ». A clear standard Arabic, lexicon of international organisations and humanitarian crises: it is the source of INT-04. The audio content of the UN news has no cost. Sources: news.un.org (page podnews.net (Podcast card, which refers to news.un.org/ar). DW Arabia. One of Deutsche Welle's four television channels (situation at 2 January 2026): 24 hours in Arabic for North Africa and the Middle East, streaming and satellite. News and in-depth programs in Arabic standard. Source: entry "DW-TV" (en.wikipedia.org). France 24 in Arabic and Monte Carlo Doualiya. The two Arabic broadcasters of the French public group France Médias Monde, which opened a regional hub in Beirut to strengthen its Arabic content. Monte Carlo Doualiya is already in Appendix C of the Volume 4. Source: Arabodonline.com ('France Médias Monde established regional hub in Beirut'); Volume 4. BBC News Arabic. The site and the television channel remain; the radio in Arabic closed in January 2023 (Volume 4, Appendix C). The sources consulted do not indicate any other changes for the 2026. Podcast in Arabic: Sowt ( ⁧صوت⁩ ) · sowt.com. Podcast network based in Amman, founded in 2017: mainly narrative programmes on social, political and cultural themes. Useful for long and long listening fuṣḥā spoken and the dialect of tale programs (B2-17); The source doesn't say in which variety the individual programs are in: listen a few minutes before choosing one. Source: entry "Sowt (podcasting) " (en.wikipedia.org). Newspapers and news sites. The course does not indicate a "right" heading: B2-19 and B2-23 They really need different warheads. Choose at least two different countries and editorial lines, a panarabas and a national one, and read the same type of news every day about both. The institutional pages (C4) are used to control figures and quotes.
C4 Institutional sources and speeches (INT-03INT-04INT-06)

UN Speech Bank · speechbank.un.org. Collection of the United Nations Department of General Assembly and Conference Management, designed to prepare interpreters and translators for the UN exams. Contains Arabic speeches with audio (mp3) and transcription to PDF; For example, the address of the United Arab Emirates Foreign Minister to the general debate of the 70to the General Assembly (2015), about five minutes. It is the ideal source for INT-06: Listen with the covered transcription, then analyze structure, protocol and figures. This is not a complete collection of UN speeches. Source: speechbank.un.org (AR_ discourse page00009). United Nations agencies in Arabic. Many agencies have pages in Arabic; UNHCR ( ⁧المفوضية السامية للأمم المتحدة لشؤون اللاجئين⁩ ), for example, has information pages in Arabic for several countries on its websites      .Help , (help.unhcr.org). They are useful for INT- vocabulary.04 and B2-20 ( ⁧لَاجِئ⁩ , ⁧طَالِبُ لُجُوءٍ⁩ ) used with technical value. Source: help.unhcr.org (pages in Arabic for Algeria, United Kingdom, United States). The League of Arab States ( ⁧جامعة الدول العربية⁩ ). For official communications and speeches (INT-03INT-06) uses the League's institutional site. The address has changed over the years and for this edition it was not possible to confirm it from a reliable source: look for it under the Arabic name, check whether it is the official website (not a site that mimics it) and note the address in the register. Rules. Copy the names of the institutions as the institution writes them; Note link and date; use consolidated Italian translation if it exists. An official discourse is a public text: analyze it as text (structure, figures, commitments and vague formulas), without judging people.
C5 · Check the news (INT-05)
Misbar ( ⁧مسبار⁩ ) · misbar.com.

• What is it: news verification platform launched in 2019, based in Jordan, Arabic and English; Today, independent non-profit organization with offices in the United States and Jordan. It also publishes the "Misbar Index" which assigns transparency scores to warheads according to the severity and frequency of misinformation.
• Advantages: many articles in Arabic, with the structure "statement · verification · verdict" of INT-05.
• Limits: the source consulted does not say if today the platform adheres to the International Fact-code.
Checking Network (he participated in the #CoronaVirusFacts alliance, concluded in 2023); like other platforms has been targeted at misinformation campaigns with false verification requests.
• Use during: INT-05, carrying out a verification exercise; B2-23, checking the figures of authentic texts.
• Source: item "Misbar" (en.wikipedia.org)
Fatabyyano ( ⁧فتبينوا⁩ ) · fatabyyano.net.

• What was: born in 2014 as Facebook page, registered in Jordan 2016; from 2023 has also a company in the United Arab Emirates. It presents itself as a platform independent of parties, with the aim of an Arabic content free from false voices and a reader that checks before sharing.
• Limits: information comes from the platform presentation page; the method page Work was not readable at the time of check.
• Use during the course: as a second source of verification, to compare two verdicts on the same news.
• Source: fatabyyano.net (page ⁧حول فتبينوا⁩ »)

AFP Fact Check in Arabic. From 2019 the agency France-Presse has a verification team in Arabic based in Beirut, born from an agreement with Facebook for the Middle East and North Africa; The articles in Arabic are published on the blog "AFP Fact Check" alongside those in English, French, Spanish and Portuguese. Source: moderanghana.com (AFP communication of 6 February 2019). How to use them. A verification platform is a source like the others: read the method, compare more verdicts, distinguish "false" from "we found no evidence" (INT-05) and records the date of verification. The verification platforms work in difficult contexts and can be subject to pressure or accusations: this is one more reason not to rely on a single source.
C6 · Egyptian
Kallimni ʿArabi Mazboot · An Early Advanced Course in Spoken Egyptian Arabic 4 Samia Louis · The American University in Cairo Press, October 2009 · ISBN 9789774162237.
• Recipients: who has already completed the intermediate Egyptian levels (the Kallimni series) ʿArabi, Volumes 3 and 4 of This course).
• Level: Early advanced, according to the publisher; matches the EGY track-11 EGY-18.

• Advantages: eight modules with two lessons each and a free conversation (saying "Chat with us"): tastes and time Free, movies and difficult experiences, guide and tell the past, hypotheses and desires, get to know each other, regrets and advice, show, work and debates; a general review; audio of dialogues and exercises recorded by Egyptian speakers; setting according to the ACTFL guidelines; 232 pages.
• Limits: in English; the editor's page does not indicate the price or writing used (Arabic or transliteration).
• Cost: not indicated on the page consulted.
• Use during the course: next to EGY-11 (recount), EGY-12 (debates) and EGY-18 (free conversation); after
B2, to keep the Egyptian.
Source: aucpress.com

Authentic material. For EGY-11 EGY-17 units indicate what to look for (personal accounts, talk shows, street interviews, comedy, podcasts, documentaries). Choose public material, short (3–5 minutes), with a theme you know; for movies and series check title by title that there are Arabic subtitles (Volume 4, Appendix C6).
C7 · Levantino and recognition of varieties

For B2-18 and B2-21 public recordings of speakers from different areas are needed: talk shows and debate programmes for Lebanese, Syrian, Jordanian and Palestinian televisions; Public interviews of Iraqi, Gulf and Maghreb speakers. The sources consulted do not allow to recommend a precise program with guarantee of continuity: the schedulers often change. Ask the tutor to choose two or three, write down channel, program and date, and remember the rule of B2-21: a hypothesis about variety, not a conclusion about the person. For the words: The Living Arabic Project (C2).
C8 · Moroccan

2M. Moroccan public television, born in 1989, now controlled by the State and subsidiary of the public broadcaster SNRT. News in Arabic, Amazigh and French; many foreign series dubbed also in darija; a radio, Radio 2M. Profit for MAG-03 (Moroccan television) and MAG-04 (The Darija of the Media). Source: Item2M Tv.. (en.wikipedia.org). Hespress ( ⁧هسبريس⁩ ) · hespress.com. One of the most visited news sites in Morocco, with editions in Arabic, French and English; born as an alternative to traditional media, it also publishes sponsored content (from 2015). For the fuṣḥā the Moroccan press and the Maghreb institutional lexicon; As with every warhead, compare it to other sources. Source: Hespress (en.wikipedia.org). Dictionaries: see C2.
C9 · External certification

The B2 It's the right time for an external feedback: the end of the course exam says you mastered the program, a certification tells you how to evaluate an independent examiner. CIMA · Certificat international de maîtrise en arabe Institut du monde arabe (IMA), Paris. Updating the Volume tab 4.
• Levels: six levels of the Common European Framework A1 Découverte a C2 "Maîtrise" is replaced by the following: on B2 It's called "Avancé"
• Tests: oral understanding (44 three-choice questions, 60 minutes, each document heard only once);

written understanding (44 questions, 60 minutes); written production (three tasks in 60 minutes: a story from images, 40–60 words; an answer to a message, 50–100 words; an argument, 50–100 words); recorded individual oral production (maximum 11 minutes: guided interview, role playing with two minutes of preparation, monologue without preparation). In all less than three hours, with a break of 15 minutes.

• Advantages: more than fifty centres in almost twenty countries, including Italy; certificate valid for three years; you can repeat, with at least 60 days between two sessions; productions corrected by two evaluators.

• Limits: the guide does not publish the thresholds of levels beyondA1; Writing tasks are much shorter than those of the examination B2 of this course, while the oral comprehension is heard only once (in the course, two).
• Cost: determined by the examination centre; the guide does not indicate any amounts.
• Use during the course: after examination B2, when the profile for skill (B2-24) is at least solid in all abilities.
Trained in particular to the unique listening (an authentic news daily, without repeating) and oral answers without preparation.

• Source: CIMA candidate guide, version 5.2 updated to 15 June 2023, published on imarabe.org (file of October 2024, still the version available at the date of check). ACTFL OPI and OPIC Language Testing International (LTI), exclusive licensee of the American Council on the Teaching of Foreign Languages.

• What is it: an individual oral interview with a certified examiner, usually by phone (OPI), or questions submitted by an avatar with registered answers and evaluated by an LTI examiner (OPIC). Many U.S. universities also use it for Arabic.
• Limits: only measure speech and use the ACTFL scale (Novice, Intermediate, Advanced, Superior,
Distinguished), not the Common European Framework; the source consulted does not indicate prices or arrangements for those who sign up privately from Italy.
• Use during the course: as an alternative or in addition to CIMA, if you need a feedback on the speech recognized in international field.
• Source: cslc.nd.edu (page "Language Assessment" of the University of Notre Dame)
C10 · Voice synthesis for scripts

As in previous volumes, the course does not indicate a specific app. For scripts in fuṣḥā use an Arabic voice and compare the result with the tutor; vocal synthesis helps to fix the rhythm of the news but does not replace listening to real broadcasts (C3). For scripts in Egyptian, Levant and Moroccan vocal synthesis is not suitable: they serve speakers of those varieties.
